newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African women demand harsh penalties for rapists.
newsitem.headline: S.African women demand harsh penalties for rapists.

text.p: A stream of gruesome rapes in South Africa has galvanised almost half of all women into demanding reinstatement of the death penalty, the country's largest consumer research company said on Monday.

South Africa has the world's worst rape rate, which Interpol says is almost three times higher than the U.S. rate and 12 times higher than Germany's. Local police reported 119.5 cases per 100,000 of the 42 million population last year.

"This year 86 percent of all South African women feel that punishments meted out to convicted rapists are ineffective and inadequate," Research Surveys, which polled women nationwide in 1994 and again in 1997, said in a statement.

Research Surveys said women's attitudes had hardened with a surge of rapes reported to police, and increasingly favoured hangings, last carried out in 1989 and scrapped by the Constitutional Court in 1995.

A total of 49 percent of black women polled wanted the death penalty for rapists, compared to 24 percent three years ago. Among white women, this had increased to 46 percent in 1997 from 29 percent in 1994, the company said.
Another 30 percent of both black and white women wanted rapists to serve life terms in prison. A further 10 percent preferred castration, Research Surveys said.
The survey was conducted among 1,600 women in 1994, and 1,000 women in 1997.
Rape has catapulted onto the national agenda, with community anger focusing on attacks against minors, who make up a third of South Africa's known rape victims.

Callers to radio phone-ins have applauded vigilantes or parents who take the law into their own hands, such as a policeman who went to a cell and shot dead the suspected rapist of his six-year-old daughter.
